Q: Why doesn’t the Binding I wrote in C# Markup take effect in Uno Platform A: 
Have you tried binding with a real DataContext instance? In C# Markup, DataContext<T>(...) only gives you a typed placeholder for bindings — it does not set the page’s DataContext. That’s why Approach 3 looks right but still fails.

Try this:

this.DataContext(TestModel.Instance, (page, vm) => page
    .Background(ThemeResource.Get<Brush>("ApplicationPageBackgroundThemeBrush"))
    .Content(new StackPanel()
        .VerticalAlignment(VerticalAlignment.Center)
        .HorizontalAlignment(HorizontalAlignment.Center)
        .Children(
            new TextBlock()
                .Text(() => vm.Text)
        )));

Also note the typo: Instace → Instance.

.Text(() => TestModel.Instace.Text) alone won’t work without a source/DataContext, because that expression builds a binding path, not a direct property read.

If you insist on imperative binding:

block.SetBinding(
    TextBlock.TextProperty,
    new Binding
    {
        Path = new PropertyPath(nameof(TestModel.Text)),
        Source = TestModel.Instance,
        Mode = BindingMode.OneWay
    });

(SetBinding needs TextBlock.TextProperty and a Binding object — not block.Text and a property name string.)

Q: How can I clone a Git repository with a specific revision/changeset? A:

Since Git (version control) 2.5.0, the feature described below can be enabled on server side with configuration variable uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant, here the GitHub feature request and the GitHub commit enabling this feature. Note that some Git servers activate this option by default, e.g., Bitbucket Server enabled it since version 5.5+. See this answer on Stack Exchange for an example of how to activate the configuration option.

For Git versions ]1.7; 2.5[, use git clone and git reset, as described in Vaibhav Bajpai's answer.

If you don't want to fetch the full repository then you probably shouldn't be using clone. You can always just use fetch to choose the branch that you want to fetch. I'm not an hg expert, so I don't know the details of -r, but in Git you can do something like this.

# Make a new blank repository in the current directory
git init

# Add a remote
git remote add origin url://to/source/repository

# Fetch a commit (or branch or tag) of interest
# Note: the full history up to this commit will be retrieved unless
#       you limit it with '--depth=...' or '--shallow-since=...'
git fetch origin <sha1-of-commit-of-interest>

# Reset this repository's master branch to the commit of interest
git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD

Q: Not equal operator doesn't return correct result A:

For SQL Server:

I think the problem is your date format. Try using ISO format (yyyymmdd) instead. Also since you are not having any time on the right, your o.orderdate should be a date type field otherwise convert it as convert(date,O.orderdate) <> Convert(date,'20081202');

Select Distinct E.empid, lastname, firstname 
From HR.Employees as E
INNER JOIN Sales.Orders as O
ON E.empid = O.empid 
Where convert(date,O.orderdate) <> Convert(date,'20081202')

Q: Splitting OpenMP threads into multiple teams over loop A:

I have numBlocks = 2 and [...] when I run top, the program shows at most 200% CPU usage.

This is expected. omp parallel num_threads(numBlocks) creates an OpenMP team of 2 threads here. omp for does not create more teams, this is just a work-sharing-loop construct. The iterations are distributed across the 2 threads.

omp_set_num_threads does not mutate the number of thread of a section. It would be actually far too dangerous (and expensive). It only affect the "subsequent parallel regions". The thing is there are non in the current team so the call is useless.

Nesting is generally not great. IMHO, it often cause a lot of issues. Tasks are meant to address them in relatively recent versions of OpenMP.

Update After changing my implementation to [...]

There are several issues in this code.

First, the omp barrier construct is not meant to wait tasks. This means the task can be executed after the function ends. This is a problem since your program specify the default(shared) clause for the tasks. The result is an undefined behaviour (e.g. crash, data corruption, or even possibly nothing visible so far). You should use omp taskwait instead for that.

More generally mixing task-based construct and worksharing ones are not a good idea. Implementations tends not to behave well with this. I propose you to replace the omp for with a omp taskloop.

I also advise you to avoid default(shared) like the plague. This is pretty dangerous (red flag IMHO). You should specify the variable that are shared explicitly since this is the one that matters when a crash or a race condition happens in your program. Copying small data is not only safer, it is also more efficient on some machines (e.g. NUMA systems). You should optimise such things later, only when the program is proved to work well. "Premature optimization is the root of all evil".

Update 2 I no longer get segfaults

Certainly because M was accessed outside its scope. This might not be the only one: blocks could certainly be too. Using taskwait instead should fix this issue.

I'm still stuck at ~200% CPU utilization

With 2 level of tasks it may be better. That being said some implementation may serialise the inner tasks. A workaround to such issue is to flatten the tasks (i.e. no nested tasks and one single taskwait).

Q: Save worksheet as PDF on Mac A:

The following method solves the problem

ActiveSheet.ExportAsFixedFormat Type:=xlTypePDF, Filename:=strFile
